name: php-src
one_liner: The actual program that runs the PHP programming language — the engine behind a huge share of the web.
buyer: Not really a product for a specific buyer; it's foundational open-source infrastructure maintained by the PHP core team, used indirectly by every hosting company and PHP-based app.
business_use_cases: A hosting company bundles the latest PHP build into its shared hosting plans, marketing faster page loads from PHP-version upgrades.
A legacy enterprise app pays a consultant to migrate from an old, unsupported PHP version to a current one to stay inside the security-support window.
A performance consultancy sells runtime-tuning audits to high-traffic PHP sites, profiling against mainline php-src behavior.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid PHP version-upgrade and migration services to companies stuck on deprecated versions.
Sell hosting plans that market 'always on latest stable PHP' as a performance and security differentiator.

steal_this: There's no weekend product in the interpreter itself — it's core language infrastructure, not a tool to wrap. The real weekend project is downstream: find one company visibly running an end-of-life PHP version and pitch a paid upgrade.
